item.title: French mayor caught in viral video clash says student protesters 'could be my children'
item.description: In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop."
item.dc:creator: Layli Foroudi
item.content:encoded: In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop." Bagayoko said he has been supporting the students in his working-class Parisian suburb and on Tuesday was asking the police not to charge. "They had decided to charge and effectively go after the students, many of whom had shown no aggressive behaviour whatsoever toward the police officers," Bagayoko, who is part of the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday at his town hall office in Saint-Denis, on the northern outskirts of Paris. In the end, the police fired tear gas at the group, including the mayor, he said. The wave of student protests, which began in [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"Paris' marginalised suburbs"], has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace French President Emmanuel Macron. There have been more than 6,000 arrests and dozens of student injuries since the protests began. Rights groups and unions accuse the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flashball guns. Authorities say hundreds of police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. The town of Saint-Denis, where poverty levels are more than double the national average, was one of the first sites of student protests in late September over overcrowded and unsanitary classrooms, teacher shortages and unequal opportunities. "Protests are not new here, they happen at every start of the academic year," Bagayoko said. "The Republican promise (of equality) — in particular for the working-class neighbourhoods, and also rural areas — is not respected." He said the government should prioritise investing in education and levy heavier taxes on billionaires. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Wednesday that the government would review demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October, but gave no details. The government has suggested that LFI politicians were behind the protests, an accusation that Bagayoko dismissed as insulting to the young protesters. A father of four, he said that "the high school children who were in the street could be my children ... it is my responsibility to be at their side."

item.title: Trading Day: Stocks, bonds in delicate dance
item.description: A sea of red swept across global stocks on Wednesday as the bond market selloff picked up again and lifted long-dated US yields to 24-year highs, although a strong 10-year Treasury auction and minutes of the Fed's last policy meeting eased some of the upward pressure on borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
A sea of red swept across global [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"stocks"] on Wednesday as the bond market selloff picked up again and lifted long-dated US yields to 24-year highs, although a strong [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"10-year Treasury auction"] and [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"minutes"] of the Fed's last policy meeting eased some of the upward pressure on borrowing costs. In [USN:L6N45S122 TEXT:"my column today"], I ask how much longer Wall Street can continue scaling fresh peaks while the bond market rout continues to push yields ever higher. It will depend on whether rising borrowing costs reflect strong growth expectations, or other risks captured by the 'term premium', which is now racing higher also. Today's Key Reads [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Fed policymakers divided over rate-hike logic in September, minutes show "] [USN:L8N45S0RJ TEXT:"Investors pick new darlings and duds as selloff rocks Europe's bond market "] [USN:L4N45R0DE TEXT:"India joins global rate-tightening wave with first hike in nearly 4 years "] [USN:L1N45S0Z3 TEXT:"IMF chief warns energy shock, growing debt and AI risks threaten global growth "] [USN:L6N45R0WM TEXT:"Hedge funds warn BoE repo reforms could backfire "] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Japan -1%, South Korea -2%. [USN:L6N45T0EA TEXT:"Europe"] -1%, [USN:L6N45T0IE TEXT:"UK"] -0.8%. [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"S&P 500 and Nasdaq"] -0.2%, Dow -0.7%. SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Industrials -2%, healthcare +1%. Caterpillar (CAT.N) -6%, SpaceX (SPCX.O) -2.6%. Moderna (MRNA.O) +5%, Micron Technology (MU.O) +4%. FX: US dollar back up to Monday's 17-month high, [USN:L4N45T025 TEXT:"euro"] at 17-month low. Euro/sterling down for 9th day, longest losing streak since Feb 2021. BONDS: European bonds back under pressure, French/German spread widens 10 bps to 138 bps. US 10y and 30y yields touch [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"fresh 24-year highs"] but cool after 10-year auction draws highest demand since 2016. US [USN:L6N45S1BF TEXT:"mortgage rates"] highest since 2023. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N45T01V TEXT:"Oil"] slips - Brent -0.5%, WTI -1.3%. Gold -1%, other precious metals -3%.

Today's Talking Points: United yet divided We know that the Fed's decision to raise interest rates last month, the first hike in three years, was unanimous. What we learned from the meeting [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"minutes"] published on Wednesday is policymakers were divided on the rationale for raising rates. Some saw it as a precautionary move to cool energy-driven price pressures or inflation expectations, others saw it as the first step in a battle against demand-driven inflation. This matters because it suggests there will be less certainty and unanimity at upcoming decisions, starting with the October 28-29 meeting. The Fed rarely does "one and done" rate hikes, so it's reasonable to assume there will be more tightening to come. But how much more, and the pace, are up for more debate. This may be what Chair Kevin Warsh wants. Market pricing suggests a rate hike this month is off the table, but remember, only a week ago it was very much on the table. Three weeks is a long way away. Term premium Fed officials — and policymakers elsewhere — will surely be looking at the bond market with an increasing sense of nervousness and unease. If the rise in yields is a function of investors pricing in strong economic growth driven by demand and investment, that's one thing. If it's because of inflation fears, that's another. But if it's being driven by the 'term premium' — the extra premium investors demand for general 'risk' — then that's more worrying. And the US term premium is beginning to rise. Rapidly. It has surged 40 bps in the last two weeks, and on Monday hit a 12-year high of 96 bps. Bank of America analysts note that the term premium is also gathering force in other key bond markets, and suggest three key factors investors should watch in Q4: US fiscal and funding issues, ECB willingness to stabilize spreads, and long-end JGB dynamics. AI spaghetti The news that [USN:L6N45S1CQ TEXT:"SpaceX"] is in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia's (NVDA.O) AI chips has shone the spotlight back on the debt, deals and spaghetti-like circular financing that's driving the artificial intelligence revolution. Investors are trying to grapple with a surge in corporate bond issuance to fund AI data center construction and investment, more than $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet debt, according to Morgan Stanley, and the bilateral loans, leases and agreements between several of the big players. A growing number of investors, including veterans like Jim Chanos, Steve Eisman and Michael Burry, warn that the circularity and opacity of it all spells danger. What could move markets tomorrow? [USN:L4N45O0LB TEXT:"Samsung"] earnings (Q3, prelim) European Central Bank chief economist Philip Lane speaks Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill speaks US Treasury sells $22 billion of 30-year notes at auction US Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include Governor Chris Waller, Minneapolis Fed's Neel Kashkari and St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem Want to receive Trading Day in your inbox every weekday morning? Sign up for my newsletter here . Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: AI wants to cure disease. It needs data first
item.description: Months after the OpenClaw frenzy, personal AI agents are looking promising again.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Months after the [USN:L4N406097 TEXT:"OpenClaw frenzy"], personal AI agents are looking promising again. The latest to join the party is OpenAI, which [USN:L1N45L06P TEXT:"unveiled"] its own personal agents, “dots,” at its annual dev day last week. Meta's Muse and the startup Instinct have both launched agents that are already gaining traction, built around reading your messages and acting on your behalf. Despite a glitchy demo, OpenAI is making the case that always-on dots can chase down a user's goals across apps on their own. It’s also trying to send a message: this isn't the same breed of agent that famously[USN:L6N45H0LE TEXT:" went rogue this summer"], infiltrating everything from Hugging Face to government websites. As someone who uses these things, I keep getting stuck on the same trade-off: how much of my personal information am I willing to hand over, for how much usefulness I get back? And sometimes, the limits aren't even up to me. Businesses are increasingly blocking these agents outright, wary of losing control over their own customer relationships. Amazon, for one, has cut off Meta's Muse from shopping on its website entirely, accusing it of pulling customer data without permission. Meta says it is acting in a secure manner. It's both a security story and a turf war: every major platform wants to own its customer relationship. This week, we dive into the next frontier AI keeps promising us — curing disease. How close are we, actually, to the AI-cures-cancer headlines? Scroll on. OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L8N3ZL1UG TEXT:"Companies cutting jobs as investments shift toward AI"] [USN:L4N45S0BH TEXT:"DeepSeek set to net over $12 billion in new fundraising, source says"] [USN:L4N45R19C TEXT:"Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models"] [USN:L6N45R0XK TEXT:"McDonald's hit with class action alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing"] [USN:L4N45T0O0 TEXT:"Existential threats join bubble fears as AI mood sobers at Singapore forums"] AI'S BIOLOGY RACE By now you've probably heard, more than once, that AI is going to help us cure cancer. But how far away are we, actually? From AI labs to pharma giants to Big Tech, everyone is betting that biology is the next holy grail of AI promises. We're in the early innings, researchers and scientists told me. And one major obstacle standing between AI and drug discovery's big breakthroughs? Data. Large language models got good by scraping the internet's text — an enormous, already-existing corpus. Biology has no equivalent. There is no "internet of cells" sitting around waiting to be ingested. "We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," Alex Rives, head of science at the nonprofit Biohub, told me. Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells; an accurate predictive model will need billions, eventually trillions. That gap — several orders of magnitude — is the real bottleneck for now, Rives said. So Biohub is trying to build that dataset from scratch, and has [USN:L6N45T078 TEXT:"rallied an unusual coalition"] to do it: the US government, Google, and Meta have joined the project, bringing total investment to $1.8 billion. Rives says the group is compressing work that would normally take decades into five years, with a first dataset expected to be ready in about a year, and usable models possible within five. Even then, the path from dataset to actual treatment is uncertain. Rives said researchers can only begin training models once the data exists, then test whether those models can accurately predict how a cell responds to change. If that works, it could help scientists pinpoint exactly which part of a diseased cell to target. Some are already taking the experiments into the physical world. Danaher, the life sciences giant, said this week it plans to launch its [USN:L4N45T0TZ TEXT:"first AI-powered autonomous research lab"] by early 2027, aiming to design, build, and test new antibodies up to eight times faster than conventional methods. Anthropic is making a similar bet. The company has quietly set up its own [USN:L6N45814Q TEXT:"wet lab"] in the Bay Area, where human scientists and AI agents work side by side. Eric Kauderer-Abrams, Anthropic's head of life sciences, told my colleague that the final test for any biology claim still has to happen on a lab bench, not inside a model. Anthropic says it isn't chasing drug discovery for now; it's targeting neglected corners of basic biology instead. While the industry waits for a full "virtual cell," it's also trying to make some corners of the predictions work today: a wave of AI companies are running virtual drug trials, simulating how an experimental medicine might perform before it ever reaches a real patient. The stakes are real. The biopharma industry spends roughly $140 billion a year on human clinical testing, and only about 12% of drug candidates ever win regulatory approval — a rate that's barely budged in decades. One startup, BioinvestGPT, says it [USN:L1N45M12V TEXT:"correctly predicted"] the outcome of five of six high-profile trials ahead of time, including, this past July, forecasting that Novartis' muscular dystrophy drug would fall short — months before the actual trial missed its goal and erased $30 billion in market value. The simulation side of this is already saving companies money and time. The "cure cancer" side is a different story — one that might require building a model that doesn't exist yet, at a scale nobody has ever attempted. Investors are pricing in the first story while trying to predict the timeline of the second.

item.title: Açúcar bruto atinge nova máxima em 19 meses; café arábica recua
item.description: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto ficou praticamente inalterado no final do pregão, a 20,83 centavos por libra-peso, após ter atingido mais cedo máxima de 21,24 centavos. * Operadores afirmaram que a alta nos preços contribuiu para a fraqueza da demanda no mercado físico. * Eles observaram que a alta foi impulsionada, em parte, pelas chuvas no Brasil, que devem reduzir a produção de açúcar nesta safra. * "As chuvas no centro-sul do Brasil retardaram a colheita, o que significa que agora parece provável que a produção de açúcar fique aquém das 39 milhões de toneladas previstas pela OIA há seis semanas", afirmou a Organização Internacional do Açúcar em um relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira * O fenômeno climático El Niño também foi visto como um fator que restringiu a produção do adoçante, particularmente na Ásia. * O preço do açúcar branco também apresentou poucas variações, ficando em US$555,70 por tonelada métrica CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em queda de 11,75 centavos, ou 3,9%, a US$2,927 por libra-peso, revertendo em grande parte os fortes ganhos da sessão anterior; o mercado havia subido 4,1% na terça-feira. * Os corretores afirmaram que o forte ritmo das exportações do Brasil, principal produtor, garantiu que haja atualmente oferta abundante. * As exportações brasileiras de café verde em setembro totalizaram 235.800 toneladas métricas, ou 3,93 milhões de sacas de 60 kg, o maior volume em 20 meses, de acordo com dados do governo divulgados na terça-feira * No entanto, as preocupações de que o fenômeno El Niño reduza a produção global na safra 2027/28 continuaram a sustentar os preços, enquanto os estoques certificados nas bolsas também permanecem baixos * O café robusta registrou queda de 2,9%, para US$ 3.485 por tonelada CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou em queda de £57, ou 1,3%, a £4.174 por tonelada. * Os corretores observaram que as chuvas previstas devem melhorar as perspectivas para as safras na Costa do Marfim, principal produtora. * "As chuvas que se aproximam vão amenizar significativamente as preocupações com a seca na principal safra de cacau da Costa do Marfim, mas podem não ser suficientes para garantir a recuperação dos frutos novos", afirmou a LSEG Research and Insights em uma nota * O cacau de Nova York recuou 2,1%, para US$5.582 por tonelada. (Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Missouri sued over alleged decades of underfunding at historically Black university
item.description: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Flowers
item.content:encoded: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades. The complaint, filed in federal court in the US District Court for the Western District of Missouri Central Division, seeks compensatory damages under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act for what plaintiffs describe as "educational and economic injuries" caused by decades of underfunding. It also seeks an injunction requiring Missouri to fully match Lincoln University's federal land-grant funding in the future. Some of the funding they are requesting would include campus repairs, faculty hiring, student services, financial aid and agricultural research programs. Lincoln University, in Jefferson City, is the state's first historically Black land-grant institution. The University of Missouri is the state's predominantly white land-grant institution. The plaintiffs allege Missouri appropriated less per student to Lincoln than to the University of Missouri in most fiscal years between 1987 and 2020. They cited a September 2023 letter in which the US agriculture and education secretaries calculated that Missouri had underfunded Lincoln by $361.6 million over that period, based on federal higher education data. According to the complaint, Missouri provided no state matching funds for Lincoln's federal land-grant allocation from fiscal 2000 through 2007, and supplied only a portion of the required match in subsequent years. Lincoln allegedly diverted about $43.5 million from its general operating budget between 2000 and 2016 to cover the state's share, and returned nearly $8 million in federal funds from 2016 through 2018 when it could not meet matching requirements. Missouri fully matched the University of Missouri's land-grant allocations during the same period, the complaint said. The University of Missouri declined to comment, citing "ongoing litigation." Lincoln University of Missouri did not respond to an immediate request for comment. The lawsuit names the State of Missouri, the state Coordinating Board for Higher Education, Governor Michael Kehoe, Higher Education Commissioner Bennett Boggs and University of Missouri System President Mun Choi as defendants. State officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit argues the funding gap perpetuates the legacy of Missouri's formerly segregated higher education system, under which the University of Missouri served white students and Lincoln was established for Black students. "Lincoln is constantly putting Band-Aids over bullet wounds because they do not have the resources to fully address the blow," Makhi Jaff, a plaintiff, said in the lawsuit. Plaintiffs include alumni who attended Lincoln in the 1980s and 1990s, a former student who left without a degree in 2024, and four current students. They describe deteriorating residence halls, limited dining and health services, scarce course offerings, inadequate advising and financial hardship. One student stated in the lawsuit that she lost weight because dining services closed before band practice ended. Another student said a scholarship she expected to cover her education was withdrawn, requiring her to take loans and work up to 30 hours weekly.

item.title: Trump dice que se merece el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero duda de que se lo concedan
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que libra una guerra contra Irán y aún no ha logrado negociar un armisticio en Ucrania, dijo el miércoles que debería ganar el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero reconoció que tenía dudas sobre sus posibilidades.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que libra una guerra contra Irán y aún no ha logrado negociar un armisticio en Ucrania, dijo el miércoles que debería ganar el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero reconoció que tenía dudas sobre sus posibilidades. "No sé cuál va a ser su decisión", dijo Trump sobre el premio de 2026, que el Comité Noruego del Nobel anunciará el viernes. "Tienen fama de no concedérselo a gente como yo". Desde su regreso a la Casa Blanca el año pasado, Trump ha dicho en repetidas ocasiones que se merece el que podría ser el premio más prestigioso del mundo. "Ya va siendo hora", dijo Trump a los periodistas en el Despacho Oval. "Pero fue un gran honor recibirlo indirectamente la última vez de manos de la galardonada, quien dijo que nadie en la historia lo merece más que el presidente Trump". La líder de la oposición venezolana, María Corina Machado, entregó su medalla del Premio Nobel de la Paz de 2025 a Trump en enero, en un intento por conseguir el apoyo de Estados Unidos a sus esfuerzos en Venezuela. Trump dijo que debería recibir el premio tras haber intervenido en ocho conflictos desde que asumió el cargo. Los líderes de Camboya, Israel y Pakistán dijeron que postularon a Trump, aunque no hay forma de verificarlo. A Trump no le ha sido posible alcanzar una solución a la guerra de Rusia en Ucrania, a pesar de que prometió ponerle fin el primer día de su segundo mandato en la Casa Blanca. Los ataques conjuntos de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán han dado lugar a un conflicto latente de siete meses que ha trastocado el suministro energético mundial y ha provocado una subida de los precios de la gasolina. El papa León, la Corte Penal Internacional y la relatora especial para los Territorios Palestinos, Francesca Albanese, estan entre los favoritos para ganar este año.

item.title: Raise a glass: League to allow drinking celebrations after 'juice' saga
item.description: NFL players will not be disciplined for celebrations that imitate drinking a beverage, the league and union said on Wednesday, after a high-profile saga involving 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk this season prompted outcry and mockery from fans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: NFL players will not be disciplined for celebrations that imitate drinking a beverage, the league and union said on Wednesday, after a high-profile saga involving 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk this season prompted outcry and mockery from fans. The NFL was once known derisively as the "No Fun League" for its hard line stance on end-zone celebrations but relaxed its rules in 2017, allowing for [USN:KCN1PQ4H5 TEXT:"elaborate dances and routines"] in a largely well-received shift. But the line between what is and is not permitted in the heat of celebration became blurred [USN:L6N45G1AA TEXT:"last month"] when Juszczyk was fined for a gesture that the NFL said imitated swigging a beer during an on-field celebration. Juszczyk, who appealed the decision, posted several examples of his drinking celebration that went unpunished, saying that the celebratory sip was a nod to his nickname "Juice." He told ESPN's NFL insider Adam Schefter : "I don't even drink beer!" "Recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline," the NFL and NFLPA said in a joint statement. Juszczyk also saw his fine rescinded on Wednesday, according to media reports. The joint statement reminded players that certain gestures, including those depicting violence, the use of weapons, smoking or drug use were not permitted. "The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules," the statement read. "When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines."

item.title: シリア、サウジへの軍事支援検討 フーシ派との戦闘激化で＝当局筋
item.description:
Timour Azhari
[リヤド ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Timour Azhari

[リヤド ７日 ロイター] - 親イラン武装組織フーシ派との戦争が激化する中、シリアがサウジアラビアへの軍事支援を慎重に検討していることが分かった。この件について説明を受けた米国当局者とシリア軍当局者が明らかにした。

情報筋によると、検討されている選択肢には、サウジを攻撃から守るための防衛支援や、イエメン暫定政府軍のフーシ派掃討を後押しするための部隊派遣などが含まれるという。

米当局者によると、サウジはシリアに対し、フーシ派と戦うための部隊の派遣を要請したという。

シリア外務省へのコメント要請に対し、あるシリア外交官は、同国はフーシ派の攻撃に直面するサウジを断固として支持するとしつつも、政府の最優先事項は内戦からの復興といった国内課題にあると述べた。

同外交官は声明で「サウジが軍事協力や専門知識の共有を要請した場合、それは公式ルートを通じて、かつ両兄弟国の関係を規定する二国間協定の枠組み内でのみ行われる」と述べた。

シリアのシャラア暫定大統領は６日にサウジの首都リヤドを公式訪問し、サウジのムハンマド・ビン・サルマン皇太子と会談した。米政府当局者によると、シャラア氏はこの会談で、サウジへの軍事支援の可能性などを協議したという。

item.title: Penguins deal D Filip Hallander to Oilers for F Spencer Stastney
item.description: In a depth trade, the Pittsburgh Penguins sent forward Filip Hallander to the Edmonton Oilers for defenseman Spencer Stastney on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In a depth trade, the Pittsburgh Penguins sent forward Filip Hallander to the Edmonton Oilers for defenseman Spencer Stastney on Wednesday. Pittsburgh general manager Kyle Dubas has traded Hallander twice and acquired him once. As general manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2020, he acquired Hallander in a trade that sent Kasperi Kapanen to Pittsburgh. Dubas then dealt Hallander back to Pittsburgh to acquire Jared McCann, who was subsequently selected by Seattle in the 2021 expansion draft. Now, Dubas has shipped Hallander north of the border. Hallander, 26, had an outstanding opening night, scoring a goal and adding two assists in Pittsburgh's 7-0 win at Philadelphia. He played 9:39 on Oct. 3 against Montreal and was a healthy scratch Monday against Winnipeg. In parts of four seasons with the Penguins, Hallander has played 18 games, recording two goals and five assists while posting a plus-8 rating. Stastney was a healthy scratch for Edmonton's first three games. The 26-year-old native of Woodridge, Ill., split time between Edmonton and Nashville last season, appearing in 66 totl games, after playing 51 games for the Predators from 2022-25. He has four goals, 15 assists and 30 penalty minutes in 117 career games. Stastney is not expected to crack the Penguins' top six defensemen but adds NHL-caliber depth to the group. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it
item.description: US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump , who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the [USN:L8N3AO23E TEXT:"Nobel Peace Prize"] but acknowledged doubt about his chances. "I don't know what their decision is going to be," Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday. "They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me." Since his return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world's most prestigious award. "It is about that time," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "But I was very honored to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump." Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gave her [USN:L5N3VQ11X TEXT:"2025 Nobel Peace Prize medal"] to Trump [USN:L1N3YG0T8 TEXT:"in January"] as she sought US support for her efforts in Venezuela. Trump said he should get the prize after wading into [USN:L1N3U8067 TEXT:"eight conflicts"] since taking office last January. The leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated Trump, though there is no way of verifying that. Parties to some conflicts Trump claims to have resolved dispute the US president's diplomatic role, and fighting has flared again in some of those regions, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the border between Cambodia and Thailand. A resolution to Russia's war in Ukraine has eluded Trump, who promised to end it on the first day of his second White House term. US-Israel strikes on Iran have led to a seven-month simmering conflict that has upended global energy supplies and driven gas prices up before November's midterm elections. Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, the special rapporteur for the Palestinian Territories, are among the favorites to win this year.

item.title: Leak exposes payments made to hacking group that has extorted millions from law firms
item.description: Leak data posted to the internet has exposed payments made to a hacking group known for extorting large sums of money from law firms, blockchain investigations firm Chainalysis said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Leak data posted to the internet has exposed payments made to a hacking group known for extorting large sums of money from law firms, blockchain investigations firm Chainalysis said on Wednesday. The findings come after an unknown party posted troves of data allegedly associated with Silent Ransom Group, a prolific cyber extortion group. The FBI warned in May that the group was stealing data from law firms with hacks and demanding millions of dollars to prevent it from being posted. The FBI says the SRG targets specific firm employees with phone calls, emails and sometimes in-person visits to gain access to victims' computers in order to enable access to targeted computer networks. A website titled "The Luna Moth Files," published earlier this week by an unknown party, posted what it alleged was troves of the group's data, including chat logs, alleged ransom demand totals, documents and other materials associated with the group's work, and dozens of cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the site's claims or data, but Chainalysis said in an X post on Wednesday that "certain leaked SRG addresses sit downstream of millions of dollars in ransomware payments that SRG has extorted from victims." Chainalysis said certain cryptocurrency addresses contained in the leaks include addresses Chainalysis was already tracking prior to the leak, including one that reflected a $10 million victim payment SRG collected in mid-2026. SRG has been alleged to be involved in hacks on prominent law firms including [USN:L6N42H14I TEXT:"Fox Rothschild"] and [USN:L6N40P0LU TEXT:"Jones Day"], Reuters has previously reported.

item.title: Peso mexicano anota pocos cambios y se mantiene por debajo de umbral de 18/dlr
item.description: El peso mexicano terminó con leves cambios el miércoles, después de moverse entre bajas y alzas durante la sesión, tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano terminó con leves cambios el miércoles, después de moverse entre bajas y alzas durante la sesión, tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos. * Los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed estuvieron divididos el mes pasado respecto de los motivos para subir las tasas de interés, mostraron el miércoles las actas del encuentro de mediados de septiembre del banco central. * Los mercados proyectan que la Fed mantendrá estables las tasas en su reunión de finales de este mes, pero descuentan un alza para diciembre. * El dólar avanzó frente a sus pares apoyado más temprano por un alza de los precios del crudo, que generó temores sobre las presiones inflacionarias, pero posteriormente cedió parte de sus alzas mientras el petróleo revertía su curso luego de que la Agencia Internacional de Energía dijo que aceleraría la liberación de reservas y daría prioridad al diésel. * Los mercados ahora aguardan la divulgación de los datos locales de inflación y las minutas del último encuentro de Banxico, que se conocerán el jueves. * La moneda local cotizaba en 17.9800 por dólar hacia el final de los negocios, con una ligera baja del 0.02%, luego de tres alzas seguidas, pero manteniéndose por debajo del umbral de las 18 unidades luego de varias semanas de un rápido deterioro que la llevó a tocar la semana pasada las [USN:L1N45N0ZE TEXT:"18.4330 unidades"], su nivel más débil desde noviembre de 2025. * "El tipo de cambio muestra una leve corrección a la baja y ya cotiza por debajo del nivel de 18.00 pesos por dólar. Sin embargo, aún sería muy prematuro decir que esto podría ser un cambio de tendencia a la baja, pues los indicadores de oscilación muestran que aún hay las presiones al alza. Por ello, no se descarta que el tipo de cambio vuelva a subir a un canal entre 18.30-18.50 pesos por dólar", dijo Banco Base. * "Al alza, las resistencias técnicas se ubican en 18.0672 y 18.4320 pesos por dólar. A la baja, los soportes clave se ubican en 17.8415, 17.6590 y 17.4766 pesos por dólar", agregó. * Mientras, la bolsa mexicana cortó su racha de tres jornadas de ganancias. El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) retrocedió un 1.01%, a 64,653.33 puntos. * Destacó un descenso del 4.25% a 361.80 pesos de las acciones del Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, GAP (GAPB.MX) , tras divulgar sus cifras de tráfico de septiembre. * "En septiembre del 2026, Gap presentó un ajuste en el tráfico total de pasajeros de 7.3% vs septiembre 2025, resultado de un retroceso en el tráfico de pasajeros nacional e internacional de 9.5% y 3.2%, respectivamente", dijo Monex, que recomendó "mantener" con un precio objetivo de 480 pesos para finales de este año. * En renta fija, el bono gubernamental mexicano a 10 años cotizó con un rendimiento del 9.391%, frente al 9.411% del cierre anterior, mientras que la deuda a 20 años ofreció un retorno de 9.804%, que se compara con el 9.839% de la sesión previa.

item.title: Glaukos says late-stage eye disease treatment shows lasting benefits after single dose
item.description: Glaukos said on Wednesday patients treated with its late-stage eye disease therapy maintained improvements in vision and corneal shape three years after a single treatment for keratoconus, a disease that can progressively distort vision.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Glaukos (GKOS.N) said on Wednesday patients treated with its late-stage eye disease therapy maintained improvements in vision and corneal shape three years after a single treatment for keratoconus, a disease that can progressively distort vision. The medtech firm said patients who received a single Epioxa treatment did not require additional intervention during the three-year follow-up period. Epioxa-treated eyes showed a 1.9-diopter improvement in maximum corneal curvature from baseline after three years, indicating sustained flattening and stabilization of the cornea. About 29% of Epioxa-treated eyes gained two or more lines on a standard vision chart, while 20% gained three or more lines from baseline. The results add to evidence supporting Epioxa, which was approved as a less invasive option for keratoconus because it does not require removal of the cornea's outer protective layer before treatment. The study included 38 eyes from 35 patients, and 92% of treated eyes completed the three-year assessment. Glaukos said there were no serious adverse events, treatment-related adverse events or treatment discontinuations linked to Epioxa during the follow-up period. Keratoconus typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood and can lead to worsening vision and, in severe cases, the need for a corneal transplant, according to Glaukos.

item.title: Maduro se enfrentará a nuevos cargos por presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses: funcionario
item.description: El expresidente Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, se enfrentarán a nuevos cargos penales en Estados Unidos por la presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos en Venezuela, dijo el miércoles un funcionario en Washington.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: El expresidente Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, se enfrentarán a nuevos cargos penales en Estados Unidos por la presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos en Venezuela, dijo el miércoles un funcionario en Washington. Los nuevos cargos podrían presentarse tan pronto como el jueves, según el funcionario, quien fue informado sobre la investigación. Maduro y Flores fueron detenidos por el ejército estadounidense en Caracas el 3 de enero y trasladados a Nueva York para responder a cargos de tráfico de drogas. Ambos se han declarado inocentes y está previsto que sean juzgados a partir del 1 de junio de 2027. Un portavoz de la Fiscalía de Manhattan, que presentó los cargos, no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Los abogados de Maduro y Flores no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. La posibilidad de nuevos cargos fue reportada inicialmente por CNN el miércoles. No se dispuso de inmediato de detalles sobre los nuevos cargos, incluidas las identidades de las presuntas víctimas de tortura. El mandato de Maduro estuvo marcado por tensiones con Estados Unidos. Washington acusó a su Gobierno de detener a estadounidenses como medida de presión para obtener concesiones, tales como el alivio de las sanciones financieras. Entre los estadounidenses clasificados por Estados Unidos como detenidos injustamente durante el mandato de Maduro figuraban cinco ejecutivos petroleros arrestados bajo cargos de corrupción. Fueron liberados en 2022 a cambio de dos sobrinos de Flores que habían sido condenados en Estados Unidos por narcotráfico. Entre los detenidos también figuraban dos exmiembros de las Fuerzas Especiales del Ejército de Estados Unidos, arrestados en Venezuela en 2020 en relación con una incursión fallida destinada a derrocar a Maduro. Fueron liberados en 2023 como parte de otro intercambio de prisioneros. Desde la captura de Maduro, Venezuela ha sido dirigida por su exvicepresidenta, Delcy Rodríguez, quien ha aumentado la cooperación con la administración de Donald Trump. Maduro, de 63 años, y Flores, de 69, han permanecido recluidos en una cárcel federal de Brooklyn. Flores tiene previsto comparecer el jueves ante un tribunal federal de Manhattan para solicitar al juez de distrito Alvin Hellerstein su excarcelación antes del juicio por motivos de salud. La fiscalía se opone a su liberación.

item.title: US proposes to boost transit funding to areas with higher marriage, birth rates
item.description: The US Transportation Department said on Wednesday it is proposing to boost grants for major transit projects by 10% in areas that have above-average marriage and birth rates and imposing strict deadlines to ensure projects remain on schedule.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The US Transportation Department said on Wednesday it is proposing to boost grants for major transit projects by 10% in areas that have above-average marriage and birth rates and imposing strict deadlines to ensure projects remain on schedule. Democrats criticized the plan, which would apply to 40 major projects already in the program that funds light rail, bus and commuter rail projects and said it could result in lower spending in cities controlled by Democrats. The Transportation Department awards about $20 billion annually in transit grants. Democrats in August criticized the agency for not awarding $1.9 billion for major transit projects. "Tying funding for transit projects to marriage rates and how many babies a woman has is the sort of bizarre and dystopian idea you’d expect in a TV show, not actual policy put forth by the U.S. government," Democratic Senator Patty Murray said on Wednesday. The projects that risk facing spending cuts include Washington's Red Line subway modernization program, Boston's Green Line subway project, an expansion of the BART train in Silicon Valley and an Austin light rail project, Murray said. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in January 2025 signed a memo giving preference for transit grants to communities with higher marriage and birth rates. Murray cited a study showing the change would likely deprive historically underfunded urban neighborhoods of funding while benefiting higher-income areas and those with larger white populations. The Transportation Department said the changes included setting strict deadlines and demanding local accountability on projects up front "so we can finally build these systems faster, better, and safer... If you want federal funding, your project needs to align with where communities and families are actually growing." Murray said the new guidance could force "transit agencies and local and state governments that have already spent years planning and designing projects to follow a whole slew of new rating and cost-share requirements." She argued it was "another attempt by the Trump administration to penalize blue states and slow down and delay transit projects." In October 2025, the Transportation Department froze billions of dollars in funding for infrastructure projects in New York and Chicago after Trump blamed a partial government shutdown on Democrats in Congress, but those decisions were overturned by judges.

item.title: 米国株式市場＝反落、米長期債利回り上昇が重し
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ７日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落。米長期債利回りが上昇する中、インフレと債務拡大を巡る懸念が再燃...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝反落、米長期債利回り上昇が重し 5:19 配信

9月25日、ニューヨーク証券取引所の取引フロアで撮影。REUTERS/Brendan McDermid

［ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落。米長期債利回りが上昇する中、インフレと債務拡大を巡る懸念が再燃した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とダウ工業株３０種は５営業日ぶり、ナスダック総合は６営業日ぶりの反落となった。

小型株で構成するラッセル２０００は１．３％下落し、大型株をアンダーパフォームした。

北海ブレント先物の清算値は１バレル＝１００ドルを上回り、米長期債利回りは一時、２４年ぶりの高水準を付けた。

イラン戦争に伴う供給懸念で原油価格が高騰し、インフレ懸念が再燃するとともに、中央銀行による利上げサイクル長期化の可能性が高まっている。こうした懸念に企業や政府の債務拡大が重なって世界的な債券売りを招き、ここ数週間、各国市場を揺さぶっている。

グローバルトのシニアポートフォリオマネジャー、トーマス・マーティン氏は「投資家は原油価格が幾分落ち着くことを期待してきた。そうなれば金利も落ち着き、株式市場の支援材料になる」と指摘。「第３・四半期は相場が弱含み、調整が入るはずだった。それが起きなかったので、ひとまず歓迎しつつ利益を確定しようという流れだ」と語った。

国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）が軽油を優先して石油備蓄の放出を加速することで合意し、原油価格が下落に転じると、株価は下げ幅を縮小した。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が７日公表した９月１５─１６日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）議事要旨では、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていたことが分かった。一部の参加者はエネルギーなどの価格ショックの影響を抑えるために必要と判断した一方、よりタカ派的な参加者は、需要主導のインフレが生じつつあることへの備えとして必要と捉えていた。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場が織り込む１０月会合での利上げ確率は１７．２％と、１週間前の３７．６％から低下している。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種では、工業の下落率が最大となった一方、ヘルスケアが上昇率トップだった。

米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が発表した先週の３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利が約３年ぶりの高水準となったことを受け、住宅株指数が２．３％、住宅建設株指数が２．９％、それぞれ下落した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は１．２％下落。年初来では８０％超上昇している。

イーロン・マスク氏率いる宇宙企業スペースＸは２．５％安。エヌビディア製半導体の購入資金として４００億ドルの調達を目指しているとの報道を嫌気した。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を３．３４対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも２．３７対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６２億１０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７５億７０００万株。

item.title: Levi Strauss lifts annual profit outlook on tariff refunds, holiday demand
item.description: Levi Strauss raised its annual profit forecast on Wednesday, after benefiting from tariff refunds, as it bets on strong holiday demand for its premium denim and sweaters.
item.dc:creator: Angela M, Danielle Kaye
item.content:encoded: Levi Strauss (LEVI.N) raised its annual profit forecast on Wednesday, after benefiting from tariff refunds, as it bets on strong holiday demand for its premium denim and sweaters. Still, the company's shares fell 2% in extended trading after it reported weaker-than-expected sales in the United States and Europe. Here are more details: Levi's received $79 million in refunds during the quarter ended August 30 for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and plans to redeploy about $60 million this year on promotions and marketing Comparable sales for its direct-to-consumer business were flat in the third quarter. CEO Michelle Gass said the business fell short of expectations as sales fell in the US, while "unseasonably" warm weather weighed on traffic in Europe The back-to-school US campaign focused too heavily on loose-fitting pants rather than popular low-rise styles, Gass said Nevertheless, the jeans maker's women's line emerged as a bright spot, driven in part by a push beyond denim into tops, skirts and dresses. Products apart from denim bottoms accounted for about half of the quarter's top-line growth, Gass said Levi's Blue Tab premium denim line grew double-digits, Gass added, as the jeans maker pushes to draw in higher-income shoppers Meanwhile, sales growth in Asia was fueled by a 13% uptick in China and new collaboration with singer Rosé The company raised its outlook for annual organic revenue growth to 6%, the upper end of its previous forecast of 5.5% to 6% It raised its forecast for full-year adjusted earnings to $1.54 to $1.56 per share, from $1.46 to $1.52 per share previously Net revenue for the quarter ended August 30 rose 4% to $1.61 billion, largely in line with estimates of $1.62 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG It earned 48 cents per share on an adjusted basis in the quarter, compared with analysts' estimate of about 36 cents per share Direct-to-consumer performance in the third quarter was softer than expected, independent retail consultant Bruce Winder said, adding that the US market remains challenging due to elevated fuel prices

item.title: Petrobras arremata 19 blocos em leilão de concessão por R$3 bi
item.description: A Petrobras arrematou 19 dos 49 blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás ofertados em leilão de Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP), em regime de concessão, nesta quarta-feira, com a oferta de aproximadamente R$3 bilhões em bônus de assinatura.
item.dc:creator: Marta Nogueira, Rodrigo Viga Gaier
item.content:encoded: A Petrobras (PETR3.SA) arrematou 19 dos 49 blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás ofertados em leilão de Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP), em regime de concessão, nesta quarta-feira, com a oferta de aproximadamente R$3 bilhões em bônus de assinatura. A empresa respondeu por quase a totalidade do valor arrecadado à União na rodada. Dos 19 blocos, a petroleira estatal levou sozinha 12 áreas na Bacia de Campos, dos quais cinco em disputas com um consórcio formado por TotalEnergies e QatarEnergy. Dois desses blocos responderam por metade de toda a arrecadação da rodada. "Fomos atrás da Bacia de Campos porque enxergamos ali potencial para coisa nova e com elevado potencial... A compra das áreas explica esse interesse", disse uma fonte da Petrobras, que preferiu ficar no anonimato, à Reuters. Os maiores bônus de assinatura do leilão foram pagos pela Petrobras, no valor de R$754,197 milhões, por cada um dos blocos C-M-115 e C-M-161, na Bacia de Campos, ambos com ágio de mais de 21.000%. Os sete demais blocos a Petrobras arrematou como operadora, com 70% de participação, em consórcio com a QatarEnergy, na Bacia do Ceará. Tanto em Campos como no Ceará, a Petrobras foi a única operadora a levar áreas. O leilão ofertou mais de 300 blocos em diversas bacias. Dentre elas também estavam Potiguar, Recôncavo, Parnaíba, Ceará, Espírito Santo e Tucano Sul. A petroleira Eneva arrematou seis blocos na Bacia do Parnaíba, onde já concentra uma importante produção de gás em diversas áreas. PetroRecôncavo arrematou dois blocos, nas bacias de Potiguar e Recôncavo. Entre as independentes, a companhia Aguila foi o destaque em número de áreas, com 12 blocos, espalhados entre Potiguar, Recôncavo e Tacutu. O leilão inteiro arrecadou pouco mais de R$3 bilhões. Um dos blocos foi arrematado após o término do leilão, quando as companhias tiveram uma nova oportunidade para fazer lances. Mais cedo, a ANP [USN:L6N45T0UZ TEXT:"também negociou"] outros sete blocos exploratórios de petróleo e gás, em um leilão de partilha do pré-sal, um número recorde diário para vendas de áreas na importante região produtora, com empresas como a Petrobras, Prio e a norueguesa Equinor buscando garantir ativos próximos de onde já operam.

item.title: Venezuela's Maduro to face new US charges over alleged torture of Americans, official says
item.description: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores are expected to face new criminal charges in the United States over allegations that Americans detained in Venezuela were tortured, a US official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: Ousted Venezuelan President [USN:L6N44P07P TEXT:"Nicolas Maduro"] and his wife Cilia Flores are expected to face new criminal charges in the United States over allegations that Americans detained in Venezuela were tortured, a US official said on Wednesday. The new charges could come as soon as Thursday, according to the official, who was briefed on the investigation. Maduro, who led Venezuela for 13 years, and Flores were captured by the US military from their home in Caracas on January 3 and brought to New York to face drug trafficking charges. They have pleaded not guilty and are scheduled to go on trial [USN:L6N43O0Z4 TEXT:"starting June 1"], 2027. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney's office, which brought the charges, declined to comment. Lawyers for Maduro and Flores did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The possibility of new charges was first reported by CNN on Wednesday. Details of the new charges, including the identities of the alleged torture victims, were not immediately available. Maduro's tenure was marked by tensions with the United States. Washington accused his government of detaining Americans as leverage to extract concessions such as relief from financial sanctions. Americans whom the US classified as wrongfully detained during Maduro's tenure included five oil executives arrested on graft charges. They were [USN:L1N3120I8 TEXT:"freed in 2022"] in exchange for two of Flores' nephews who had been convicted in the US of drug trafficking. Others detained included two former US Army Special Forces members who were arrested in Venezuela in 2020 in connection with a botched raid aimed at ousting Maduro. They were [USN:S0N3BU02L TEXT:"freed in 2023"] as part of another prisoner swap. Since Maduro's capture, Venezuela has been led by his former vice president, Delcy Rodriguez, who has increased cooperation with the Trump administration. Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been held in a federal jail in Brooklyn. Flores is due to appear in Manhattan federal court on Thursday to urge US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to release her from jail before trial for health reasons. Prosecutors oppose her release.

item.title: Wall Street fecha em baixa, com rendimentos do Tesouro em alta
item.description: Wall Street fechou em baixa nesta quarta-feira, à medida que os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA de longo prazo retomaram sua alta, reacendendo os temores sobre a inflação e o aumento da dívida, um dia após o S&P 500 e o Nasdaq atingirem recordes de fechamento.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street fechou em baixa nesta quarta-feira, à medida que os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA de longo prazo retomaram sua alta, reacendendo os temores sobre a inflação e o aumento da dívida, um dia após o S&P 500 e o Nasdaq atingirem recordes de fechamento. Os três principais índices acionários dos EUA registraram quedas modestas, com o S&P 500 e o Dow Jones encerrando sequências de quatro dias de alta. O Nasdaq registrou seu primeiro dia de queda em seis. O Russell 2000, índice de pequenas capitalizações (.RUT) , apresentou desempenho inferior ao das empresas de maior capitalização, caindo 1,3%. Na esteira da alta do mercado de ações na terça-feira, o petróleo Brent ultrapassou brevemente a marca de US$100 por barril, e o rendimento dos títulos do Tesouro de longo prazo atingiu a maior alta em 24 anos. Preocupações com o abastecimento relacionadas à guerra no Irã têm levado à alta vertiginosa dos preços do petróleo, o que, por sua vez, reacendeu os temores de inflação e aumentou as chances de um ciclo prolongado de aumentos nas taxas de juros pelo banco central. Essas preocupações, combinadas com os crescentes níveis de endividamento corporativo e soberano, causaram uma onda de vendas de títulos globais, o que abalou os mercados globais nas últimas semanas. Os investidores “vêm buscando algum alívio no preço do petróleo, o que traria algum alívio nas taxas e, portanto, ajudaria o mercado de ações”, disse Thomas Martin, gestor sênior de carteiras da GLOBALT em Atlanta. “O terceiro trimestre deveria ter sido o trimestre mais fraco do ano; esperávamos uma correção”, acrescentou Martin. “Isso não aconteceu, então vamos comemorar e realizar alguns lucros.” As ações reduziram as perdas depois que os preços do petróleo bruto caíram, na sequência do acordo da Agência Internacional de Energia para acelerar a liberação de estoques de petróleo, priorizando o diesel. A ata da reunião de política monetária de setembro do Federal Reserve, na qual o banco central aprovou por unanimidade seu primeiro aumento da taxa de juros desde julho de 2023, revelou divergências quanto à justificativa do aumento. Alguns participantes consideraram o aumento necessário para conter o impacto dos choques nos preços da energia, enquanto outros acharam que o aumento era necessário para conter a inflação impulsionada pela demanda. Atualmente, os mercados financeiros estão precificando uma probabilidade de 17,2% de que o Fed implemente um segundo aumento consecutivo das taxas ao final de sua reunião de outubro, uma queda em relação aos 37,6% registrados há uma semana, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. “As expectativas do mercado em relação ao Fed vão oscilar à medida que novos dados forem surgindo”, disse Martin. “Ainda há expectativa de mais aumentos nas taxas, mas não será necessariamente um aumento a cada reunião, e é isso que o mercado está indicando; outubro será uma pausa.” O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) caiu 0,66%, para 51.180,17 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) perdeu 0,22%, para 7.801,75 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) recuou 0,22%, para 27.538,69 pontos. Entre os 11 setores do S&P 500, o setor industrial (.SPLRCI) sofreu a maior queda percentual, enquanto as ações do setor de saúde (.SPXHC) lideraram os ganhos. Na esteira da alta nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro de referência, a taxa fixa de hipotecas de 30 anos disparou na semana passada para o maior nível em quase três anos, de acordo com a associação do setor hipotecário dos EUA Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA). O setor imobiliário (.HGX) e as construtoras (.SPCOMHOME) recuaram 2,3% e 2,9%, respectivamente. As ações de empresas de chips (.SOX) , que subiram mais de 80% neste ano, caíram 1,2%. A SpaceX (SPCX.O) perdeu 2,5% após reportagens da mídia indicarem que a empresa aeroespacial de Elon Musk estava buscando US$40 bilhões em financiamento para custear a compra de chips da Nvidia. Na próxima semana, espera-se que a temporada de divulgação dos resultados do terceiro trimestre comece para valer, com uma série de grandes bancos prestes a divulgar seus resultados. É provável que os investidores analisem minuciosamente até que ponto os gastos maciços com tecnologia de IA estão começando a mostrar resultados, ao mesmo tempo em que ficam atentos a indícios sobre a saúde do consumidor norte-americano em um momento de crescentes pressões inflacionárias. Atualmente, os analistas esperam um crescimento dos lucros do S&P 500 de 30,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, de forma agregada, para o período de julho a setembro, de acordo com a LSEG.

item.title: Fed minutes show some officials want to prepare for market stress
item.description: Federal Reserve meeting minutes from last month’s policy meeting noted some officials believe it’s time for the central bank to get ready for bond market stress.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve meeting minutes from last month’s policy meeting noted some officials believe it’s time for the central bank to get ready for bond market stress. “Regarding balance sheet policy, a few participants observed that Treasury markets had been functioning smoothly but noted the importance of planning for market stress,” the [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"minutes"] from the central bank’s September 15-16 Federal Open Market Committee meeting said. These unnamed central bankers “suggested strengthening the Federal Reserve's strategy, communications, and tools for addressing market dysfunction, should it occur, while limiting the Federal Reserve's footprint in the Treasury market.” Those comments came from minutes that described central bank deliberations during a period of market unrest. Officials raised rates at last month’s meeting, boosting them by a quarter percentage point to between 3.75% and 4%, as they tightened policy to contend with high levels of inflation. Officials also penciled in another rate increase by year’s end. The shift in the path of monetary policy has been attended by a sharp rise in government bond yields that breached key levels and generated notable real-world increases in things like [USN:L6N45S1BF TEXT:"mortgage borrowing costs"]. Fed officials have been attributing the rise in yields to a solid economic outlook, the impact of strong tech investment that’s caused government yields to rise to compete for investment, and geopolitical concerns. That said, the power of the move has caused some to worry about the state of the market in a time of huge government deficits and ongoing worries about the outlook for inflation. These worries brush up against the Fed’s balance sheet because in the last two decades the central bank has addressed big periods of market stress with bond buying. The Fed dealt with the initial phases of the COVID-19 pandemic with big purchases of Treasury and mortgage debt before it transitioned those operations to a form of stimulus, for example. BALANCE SHEET BALANCING ACT That kind of buying swells the size of the Fed’s balance sheet. But new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is opposed to large Fed holdings and would like the balance sheet to be [USN:S8N40E0AX TEXT:"smaller"]. He’s named a task force to consider ways that might make that happen. The comment in the meeting minutes “sounds like an oblique way to draw a line in the sand and signal to the market and the White House that the Fed's thinking has not changed: It would intervene only if policy transmission is threatened, not simply because yields are rising rapidly,” said Derek Tang, an analyst at Monetary Policy Analytics, Inc. He added that even if the Fed does step in, it would use tools like its liquidity-providing standing repo operations and the discount window as its first line of defense against an unsettled market. Notably, those two tools are in place and are essentially on autopilot, ready to respond to market needs as they emerge. Meanwhile, Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US rates strategy at TD Securities, said he sees the comment from the minutes directed at managing technical Treasury bill buying aimed at bolstering reserve levels. “Given that we tend to see some stresses heading into year-end, this may be the discussion of resuming [Reserve Management Purchases] in the next few months,” he said, adding, “we think the Fed may resume RMP at a modest pace before year-end to ensure everything is functioning smoothly.“ In an interview last week, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari cast doubt on the need for any broad central bank involvement in the bond market in the current situation. “I see every indication that the Treasury market is functioning fine, so I'm not seeing a financial stability risk, and I don't see any reason why the Fed would intervene, given that the market appears to be functioning just fine,” the official said.

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ急落、仏財政懸念で ドルはＦＯＭＣ議事要旨後も堅調
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ７日 ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ユーロが急落した。財政懸念からフランス国債が改...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ急落、仏財政懸念で　ドルはＦＯＭＣ議事要旨後も堅調 4:40 配信

2026年3月24日撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

［ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター］　 - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ユーロが急落した。財政懸念からフランス国債が改めて売り圧力にさらされたことが背景。ドルは直近の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）議事要旨公表後に上げを維持した。

ユーロは０．５３％安の１．１１９８ドルに下落し、５日に付けた１７カ月ぶり安値に迫った。

ユーロ圏金融・債券市場では、フランスとイタリアの国債利回りが急上昇した。

マネックスＵＳＡ（ワシントン）のシニアトレーディングディレクター、フアン・ペレス氏は「欧州の問題は、しばらくの間、歳出を膨らませる一方で歳入をあまり増やさない福祉国家型の運営を続けてきたことで、それがついに重荷になってきた点だ。見通しは良くない」と述べた。

主要通貨バスケットに対するドルの値動きを示すドル指数は０．３２％高の１０２．２４。ＦＯＭＣ議事要旨公表を受けて一時上昇幅を縮めたものの、その後持ち直した。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が７日公表した９月１５─１６日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）議事要旨によると、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていた。

ドルはエネルギー価格が高止まりしていることにも支えられた。ただ原油価格は、不安定な値動きの中で序盤の上昇幅を失った。ペレス氏は「エネルギー資源へのアクセスが困難な局面で米ドルが急伸するという力学は、すでにある程度理解している」と述べた。

ＣＭＥのフェドウォッチによると、今月下旬のＦＯＭＣで少なくとも２５ｂｐの利上げが実施される確率は１９．４％と、１週間前の約３８％から低下した。一方、１２月のＦＯＭＣでの利上げ確率は８３％と織り込まれている。

英ポンドは対ドルで０．４２％安の１．３２１６ドル。一方、対ユーロでは２０２５年６月以来の高値を付けた。

対円では、ドルが０．０９％安の１５７．９５円となった。

item.title: トランプ氏、ＦＲＢは米の「低迷」望むと主張 住宅ローン金利上昇巡り
item.description: [７日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は７日、約３年ぶりの高水準となっている米３０年物住宅ローン金利に関する記者団...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トランプ氏、ＦＲＢは米の「低迷」望むと主張　住宅ローン金利上昇巡り 4:36 配信

トランプ米大統領（左）とウォーシュＦＲＢ議長。5月22日、ホワイトハウスで撮影。REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst/File Photo

[７日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は７日、約３年ぶりの高水準となっている米３０年物住宅ローン金利に関する記者団の質問に対し、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は「米国の低迷」を望んでいると主張した。

トランプ大統領は、ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長を「素晴らしい」と評する一方、他の当局者らについては「この国が低迷することを望んでいる」と批判し、「私見では、金利は下がるべきだと考えている」と述べた。

大統領執務室に同席したベセント財務長官は、高インフレの要因に「エネルギーショック」を挙げ、「イラン紛争が収束すれば、エネルギー市場は十分な供給を確保できるようになる」と指摘。そうなれば、米経済は「ＦＲＢの目標に向かって動き始め、住宅ローン金利や１０年債利回りは再び低下するだろう」との認識を示した。

Trump to appear at White House science event on Thursday

Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX and owner of X, formerly known as Twitter, speaks during National Design Studio's launch event for America.gov, a new AI-powered government website, at the Mellon Auditorium in Washington, D.C., US, September 29, 2026. REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 7 : US President Donald Trump will speak at a White House event on scientific discovery on Thursday, according to a social media post from his tech adviser Michael Kratsios. The event will highlight the Trump administration's plan to overhaul how federal scientific research funding is managed and distributed, according to an invitation seen by Reuters. Kratsios first released the plan in July. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will also speak at the event, according to the invitation and a post from Kratsios on the social media platform X.  Trump will separately award the National Medal of Science on Thursday to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su, a White House official said in a statement. The National Medal of Science is the nation's highest honor for scientists and engineers, according to the US National Science Foundation's website. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the White House official said. That is the nation’s highest honor for technological achievement, according to the US Patent and Trademark Office's website.

Source: Reuters

item.title: CDC considera baixo o risco de peste e monitora chegadas da Sibéria, diz diretora
item.description: A diretora do Centro de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) dos Estados Unidos, Erica Schwartz, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que o risco decorrente de um caso não confirmado de peste pneumônica na Sibéria é extremamente baixo para os EUA, mas a agência está preparada para monitorar e fazer uma triagem dos viajantes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A diretora do Centro de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) dos Estados Unidos, Erica Schwartz, afirmou nesta quarta-feira que o risco decorrente de um caso não confirmado de peste pneumônica na Sibéria é extremamente baixo para os EUA, mas a agência está preparada para monitorar e fazer uma triagem dos viajantes. “Estamos trabalhando com o Departamento de Segurança Interna, com o Departamento de Estado, o Departamento de Guerra e outras agências do governo para garantir que saibamos exatamente se alguém daquela região entrar nos Estados Unidos”, disse Schwartz no evento “O Futuro da Saúde”, organizado pelo Wall Street Journal em Washington. O CDC possui um posto de saúde no Aeroporto Internacional John F. Kennedy que pode realizar vigilância e triagem de viajantes da região que entram nos Estados Unidos, acrescentou. O Departamento de Saúde e Serviços Humanos (HHS, na sigla em inglês) dos EUA não respondeu imediatamente se a agência planeja estabelecer triagem no JFK. Um porta-voz do HHS disse que cerca de 200 pessoas por ano procedentes da região da Sibéria viajam para os Estados Unidos. Os voos diretos entre a Rússia e os Estados Unidos estão suspensos desde o início da guerra na Ucrânia, em 2022. O órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia afirmou que não há riscos de uma epidemia na Sibéria após a morte de uma funcionária do instituto de peste local por pneumonia de origem ainda não determinada, em um caso que gerou preocupação internacional. “O que estamos fazendo, de uma perspectiva governamental ampla, é garantir que entendamos exatamente qual é essa ameaça”, disse Schwartz. “Estamos muito confiantes de que a ameaça para os Estados Unidos é extremamente baixa.” O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, também disse a jornalistas não acreditar que a morte tenha sido causada por uma arma biológica.

item.title: 米台関係、米中首脳会談後も強固 防衛装備の適時引き渡し重要＝駐米代表
item.description:
David Brunnstrom
[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
David Brunnstrom

[ワシントン　７日　ロイター] - 台北駐米経済文化代表処のアレクサンダー・ユー代表（駐米大使に相当）は７日、先月の米中首脳会談後も米台関係は引き続き強固との認識を示し、米国による防衛装備品の適時の引き渡しが重要になると強調した。

トランプ米大統領は９月２４日に中国の習近平国家主席をホワイトハウスに迎え、国賓待遇で首脳会談を実施。トランプ氏は習氏との良好な関係を優先し、台湾に対する総額１４０億ドル規模の新たな武器売却計画の承認を見送っている。

ユー代表はワシントンで開かれたシンポジウムで、米政府は対台湾政策に変更はないと明確に示しているとし、「米台関係は依然として強固だと自信を持って言える」と述べた。

その上で、平和を維持する最も効果的な方法は力による抑止だとし、「侵略が容易でも低コストでもないとの認識を確実にすること」が重要になると指摘。「抑止力に信頼性を持たせるためには、台湾自身の投資に加え、装備品の適時引き渡しや効果的な訓練、それらの投資を実際の抑止力へと結び付ける能力が必要になる」と語った。

最新鋭のＦ１６戦闘機の最初の２機がこのほど台湾に引き渡されたことについて、台湾の自衛能力強化に向けた米国との協力が着実に進展している好例だと指摘。「今後も米台協力はこうした取り組みの中核であり続ける」と述べた。

ロイターは今月、中国の習主席は必要に応じて２０２７年までに台湾を武力で掌握できる態勢を整えるよう軍に指示しているものの、米政府当局者の間では２８年以前の中国による台湾侵攻の可能性は低下しているとの見方が強まっていると報道。

これに関連してユー氏は「２７年、もしくは２８年以降など、さまざまな見方が出ているが、われわれの責任は変わらない。台湾をより強く、より強靱にし、敵対勢力による威圧を受けにくくすることだ」とし、台湾の防衛態勢はある特定の時期を前提に構築されているわけではないと語った。

現在、台湾の林佳龍外交部長（外相）と蔡英文前総統が米国を訪問中。林氏は同シンポジウムで行ったビデオ演説で、台湾と米国は半導体、人工知能（ＡＩ）、サプライチェーン（供給網）安全保障などの分野で協力を深めており、「真の共生関係」にあるパートナーになったと指摘。台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が米アリゾナ州で進める投資に言及し、こうした投資は経済的な結び付きが共通の利益と長期的な信頼関係の醸成につながっていると述べた。

item.title: US will rescind policy targeting oil and gas industry methane leaks
item.description: The US Environmental Protection Agency said on Wednesday it would soon propose scrapping a Biden-era rule aimed at curbing large leaks of methane from oil and gas operations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Environmental Protection Agency said on Wednesday it would soon propose scrapping a [USN:L1N3CW2NF TEXT:"Biden-era rule"] aimed at curbing large leaks of methane from oil and gas operations. The move is part of a broad Trump administration effort to slash regulations that it says burden US businesses as it seeks to boost fossil fuel production. "Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work. They can’t do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens," EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said in a statement after making the announcement at a meeting with oil and gas industry representatives in New Mexico. EPA's "super emitter" program requires companies to react when third parties report suspected methane leaks using remote sensing. The Trump administration, after taking office last year, had delayed implementation of the policy until next year. EPA said its proposal to rescind the rule would save $45 billion a year. [USN:L1N2RT11T TEXT:"Methane"] is the second-biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide, and the oil and gas industry is a major source of the gas. Environmental groups criticized the move. "This giveaway to fossil fuel executives is foolish and short-sighted, and reveals who the Trump administration really works for - its political donors,” Mahyar Sorour, director of the Sierra Club's Beyond Fossil Fuels campaign, said in a statement.

item.title: Spanish woman whose eviction ignited housing protests dies at 87
item.description: Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old Spanish woman whose dramatic eviction last month sparked mass housing protests that led to an early election, has died, the Madrid tenants' union said on Wednesday, as thousands demonstrated over her death.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Lombardi, Corina Pons
item.content:encoded: Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old Spanish woman whose [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"dramatic eviction"] last month sparked mass housing protests that led to an early election, has died, the Madrid tenants' union said on Wednesday, as thousands demonstrated over her death. Abascal had been in hospital for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her eviction on September 23 from her home of more than 70 years, when police and social workers removed her by stretcher. Her case ignited protests over a mounting housing crisis including a shortage of homes and surging rents. Activists camped out in a major Madrid square. Following news of Abascal's death on Wednesday, thousands marched from the square, Puerta del Sol, towards parliament, chanting: "This is not a death. It's a murder!" A cause of death was not announced. "This was a completely avoidable death that symbolizes the drama that is the housing crisis in Spain," said 36-year-old marcher Dario Gomez in Madrid. Demonstrators also held protests in Barcelona. Trade unions on Wednesday [USN:L1N45T0BN TEXT:"announced"] a nationwide general strike over housing issues on November 11. The protests, along with [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"parliament's rejection last week"] of decrees aimed at curbing evictions and limiting rent pressures, prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call an [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"early election"] for November 29. Sanchez is seeking to shift the political narrative from his government's [USN:L1N4510WI TEXT:"handling of a migrant crisis"] in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta and a [USN:L1N42U0KB TEXT:"series of corruption cases"] involving his Socialist Party and his family to the housing crisis, hoping to tap into growing resentment over rising rents. "Now, following her passing, we are left with the example of the fight she waged and the legacy Maricarmen has left behind. And, above all, we will honour what she always asked of us: 'Fight, keep fighting for what is yours,'" the tenants' union said in a statement. Sanchez lamented Abascal's death in an X post. "A hug as well to all of us who feel this loss as our own today," he wrote. The leader of Spain’s centre-right opposition People’s Party, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, said on X that Abascal's death shouldn't be politicised. There should be "no campaigns, no political parties, no other interests here," he wrote. "In the face of someone’s death, respect is all that matters.” HOUSE BOUGHT BY INVESTMENT FUND Abascal was evicted after an investment fund bought her house. Several days later, her lawyer said she reached an eight-year agreement with her landlord that would allow her [USN:L1N45J05P TEXT:"to return home"] and pay rent at the same prior amount. She had planned to sign the deal once she felt better, but never had the opportunity to leave hospital. A neighbour of Abascal, whose home was near Madrid's famed Retiro Park, said she was shaped by living through Spain's authoritarian Franco regime, which ended in 1975. "She was a fighter, with very clear ideas, a somewhat broad sense of justice, and, above all, perhaps a social conscience and ideas about solidarity," he said. Guillermo Ruiz, 31, an audiovisual specialist at the mass march, said he felt pessimistic about change. "The best homage we can pay to her is to continue the fight, continue to mobilise, fight for a dignified life and that what happened to her doesn't happen to anyone else."

item.title: Anglo-Teck merger, nickel sale are test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities, CEO says
item.description: Anglo American’s proposed US$54 billion merger with Canada’s Teck Resources and the sale of its Brazilian nickel business have become test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities as they await ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: JOHANNESBURG -- Anglo American’s proposed US$54 billion merger with Canada’s Teck Resources and the sale of its Brazilian nickel business have become test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities as they await antitrust approval, CEO Duncan Wanblad said on Wednesday. The Anglo-Teck merger, announced in 2025, has received approval from all countries where the companies operate except China. Both expect the deal to close by March 2027. Critical minerals have become a flashpoint in global competition, with major economies seeking to secure supply chains for electric vehicles, renewable energy and defence. China’s antitrust regulator has asked Anglo American to commit to supplying the country with a steady flow of copper concentrate as a condition for approving the merger, three people aware of the development said. Geopolitical shifts, supply chain disruptions and critical mineral nationalism have created a complex environment for such deals, Wanblad told a mining conference in Johannesburg via video link. ‘In new waters’ “We are in new waters. We are pioneering in a way. I genuinely don’t think from an antitrust perspective there should be any issues with any of these deals,” Wanblad said. He cited Anglo’s proposed sale of its Brazilian nickel business to MMG, which drew a warning from the European Union over concerns the Hong Kong-listed miner could divert supply away from Europe, hurting stainless steel producers there. The sale is awaiting EU approval. Anglo American also agreed to sell its steelmaking coal mines in Australia to U.K.-based miner Dhilmar for up to $3.88 billion. “We are kind of the guinea pigs for the market in terms of working this out,” Wanblad said. Wanblad also said he was hopeful the sale of diamond company De Beers would be completed by the end of this year. The sale of the assets is part of Anglo’s restructuring aimed at focusing on copper and iron ore. The Teck merger would expand Anglo’s copper portfolio, positioning it as the fifth-largest producer of the metal critical to the energy transition. (Reporting by Nelson Banya and Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo; Editing by Rod Nickel)

item.title: イエメン戦闘激化、フーシ派がサウジ2空港攻撃 3人死亡
item.description: [７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[７日　ロイター] - イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアが支援するイエメン暫定政府軍との戦闘が激化している。イエメン運輸省は、フーシ派が７日未明、南部の港湾都市アデンの国際空港を弾道ミサイルと爆発物搭載ドローン（無人機）で攻撃したと発表した。

一方、サウジアラビア民間航空当局は７日、国内の２空港が攻撃を受け、３人が死亡し、３６人が負傷したと明らかにした。

当局の声明によると、攻撃は６日と７日に発生。首都リヤドのキング・ハーリド国際空港では１人が死亡、８人が負傷、アブハ国際空港では２人が死亡、２８人が負傷した。どちらの空港がどちらの日に攻撃を受けたかは明らかにしていない。

米国とイランの紛争が波及した今回の戦闘は、世界最悪の人道危機の一つにつながったイエメンでの１２年間にわたる内戦を再燃させた。国連の国際移住機関（ＩＯＭ）のデータによると、フーシ派とイエメン暫定政府軍との戦闘を受け、イエメン国内では７日時点で２０万人以上が避難を余儀なくされたことが分かった。

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（7日）
item.description: ＜ロンドン株式市場＞ 反落して取引を終えた。銀行株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４営業日ぶりに反落。債券利回りの急上昇が相...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（7日） 3:33 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞　反落して取引を終えた。銀行株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４営業日ぶりに反落。債券利回りの急上昇が相場の重荷となった。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は反落し、０．７４％安。    英３０年債利回りは約２８年ぶりの高水準を付けた。英ポンドは対ユーロで約１年４カ月ぶりの高値を付けた。     ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は３．９０％安。スタンダード・チャータードは４．５％、バークレイズは３．４％それぞれ下落した。ＨＳＢＣは４．４％安。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズは、ＨＳＢＣが人工知能（ＡＩ）導入推進の一環として英国のウェルス・マネジメント事業で大規模な人員削減を計画していると報じた。    石油大手のシェルは、７─９月期の精製マージンが４─６月期を大幅に上回る見通しを示したものの、０．１％安だった。    上下水道・廃棄物処理のペノン・グループは２０．１％安。新株発行による増資と配当減を発表し、売りが膨らんだ。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　４営業日ぶりに反落して取引を終えた。長期金利の上昇を受け、投資家にリスク回避の姿勢が強まった。ドイツの１０年債利回りは一時３．５２７９％まで上昇。フランスの財政を巡る懸念も続いている。    ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種銀行株指数は３．３１％、テクノロジー株指数は１．８９％それぞれ下落。ＵＢＳが投資判断を引き下げたオランダの半導体組立装置メーカー、ＢＥセミコンダクターは８．５％安だった。    自動車・部品株指数は０．３３％安。欧州連合（ＥＵ）が中国製ハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）の域内への輸入制限を検討していると伝わり、買い優勢となる場面もあった。    上下水道・廃棄物処理のペノン・グループは２０．１％安。新株発行による増資と配当減を発表し、売りが膨らんだ。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　フランスとイタリアの国債利回りが急上昇した。エネルギー価格の上昇を背景に世界的な債券売り圧力が高まる中、一部のユーロ圏諸国の高水準の債務に対する懸念が意識された。    フランス１０年債利回りは１２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の４．８７％。取引時間中に１８ｂｐ上昇する場面もあった。フランス国債は、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比５％を超える広範な財政赤字と、来年実施される大統領選挙を巡り投資家が懸念を強める中、欧州における債券売りの中心となっている。    独仏１０年債利回り格差は１３６ｂｐと６ｂｐ拡大。同利回り格差は先週、２０１２年以来の高水準となる約１６０ｂｐを付けていた。    イタリア１０年債利回りは１１ｂｐ上昇の４．６４６％と、２３年１０月以来の高水準に迫った。    安全資産を求める動きが見られる中、ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは３．４８４％と横ばいで推移。    一方、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りはＥＣＢの利上げ観測が後退する中、４ｂｐ低下の３．０４２％となった。

item.title: Trump administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorization
item.description: The US Department of Homeland Security has proposed that international students pay at least $70,000 in training fees if they want to work in the country, ...

Trump administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorization

Reuters

08 October, 2026 12:00 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+
